text:
maya: Heads-up — multiple tickets about console charts timeout and slow initial load after yesterday's frontend deploy. Seeing ~3s extra on dashboard open. :frowning:
eric: ugh. do we have any perf telemetry traces? heatmap/median?
maya: sent a quick flamegraph from the user's session (San Francisco prod) — attaching snippet:
maya: ```
Main bundle parse+eval: 420ms
Hydration: 1.8s
Chart render (large timeseries): 950ms
Total TTFI: ~3.2s
``` 
jordyn: that matches the automated APM alerts I saw — spike at 15:42 UTC correlated with frontend v2.14.0 rollout
console-bot: deploy v2.14.0 -> 1760876000 completed, rollout: 100% (canary 10% at 15:26)
samir: note we also shipped the new unified charting component (ux/charts) and bumped recharts -> 3.8.1. bundle size +120KB gz
olivia: could be the new chart code doing synchronous layout? any long tasks in lighthouse trace?
eric: Lighthouse from one affected session shows a 1.9s long task for "rendering" caused by canvas drawing + serialization
maya: repro steps: open console, select project, go to Observability > Token-level chart, wait 2-3s for metrics. repro is consistent on Chrome 114 on mac.
jordyn: quick hypothesis list: 1) bundle size increase (parse/eval) 2) sync chart render on mount 3) lost memoization after prop shape change
samir: I ran bundle analyzer on the prod build — ux/charts pulls in moment-duration-format and a heavy dependency tree from recharts utils. here's the chunk: 
```
vendors~ux-charts.js  142KB gz
main.js  320KB gz
```
so chunking could help
olivia: short-term mitigations: revert v2.14.0, or rollback chart lib upgrade. Long-term: code-split charts, lazy-load, and server-side downsampling for large timeseries.
maya: ops question: is immediate rollback possible without touching infra? we could rollback via console rollout feature and flip to v2.13.9
eric: we have a canary rollback button in console -> I can flip it to 0% canary to stop new sessions, but sessions already routed will keep the bundle cached in browser.
samir: also consider adding runtime check to avoid rendering full-resolution data until after hydration: e.g., show placeholder + progressive hydrate.
jordyn: I sketched a small patch to lazy-load the heavy chart bundle:
jordyn: ```js
const Chart = lazy(() => import('./charts/HeavyChart'))
return <Suspense fallback={<SkeletonChart/>}><Chart data={downsampled}/></Suspense>
``` 
jordyn: reduces main bundle parse time by ~380ms in my local profile
olivia: +1 for lazy-load. also we should add a telemetry event for chart bundle load + render time so we can measure impact per release
maya: agree. can we get a canary experiment (50/50) with the lazy-load change and measure? chart load and TTFI as metrics.
eric: I can wire the experiment via rollout flags. Need a PR and a short changelog
samir: also let's add caching headers for static chunks on CDN (immutable) to reduce repeat parse cost for returning users
maya: plan: 1) jordyn opens PR for lazy-load + skeleton (tag: WIP) 2) eric creates 50/50 canary via rollout flags 3) samir configures CDN caching for vendors~ux-charts chunk 4) olivia adds telemetry events (chart.chunk.load, chart.render.ms) 5) monitor for 1h then decide rollback vs promote
maya: timeline? can we land the PR and experiment within 2 hours?
jordyn: I'll open PR in 10m. initial perf numbers attached in the PR description.
eric: I'll prepare the rollout and smoke test checklist
olivia: I'll add telemetry and a small dashboard showing median render time by release channel
maya: thanks team — please post updates here. :eyes:
jordyn: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/3281 — WIP, includes lazy-load + skeleton + downsampling util
samir: CDN config PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infrastructure/pull/912 — sets immutable cache for vendors~ux-charts chunk
olivia: telemetry PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/421 — emits chart.chunk.load and chart.render.ms (client side)
eric: rollout created: 50% traffic to lazy-load experiment at flag=chart_lazy_50 — monitoring now
maya: initial results after 12m: users in experiment show median console open TTFI down 850ms. non-experiment unchanged. :tada:
jordyn: sweet, looks promising. let's keep experiment for 1h then we can promote. also need to run a smoke on mobile
maya: thanks everyone — leaving notes for oncall: if errors spike, we rollback to v2.13.9 and revert flag
olivia: filed followups: add unit tests for skeleton fallback, add integration test that validates telemetry emitted
samir: created ops runbook snippet for future regressions (bundle-analyze -> lazy-load -> telemetry) in docs repo
maya: closing the thread for now, will update when we promote. :shipit:
